Q: Sourcetree not running external tool after macOS update A:

Sourcetree configures the external diff in the menu Sourcetree > Settings > Diff

Try flip-flopping the Visual Diff Tool selection so you get the right current path. Note that bash was replaced as the default shell by zsh in MacOS 14 so any custom commands you had might have had may now be invalid in MacOS 26.

As of Sourcetree v4.2.16 the external diff tool is launched correctly in opendiff/FileMerge and kdiff3

though switching to kdiff3 seemed to require relaunching Sourcetree after selection.

Q: There is any way to use C++23 print() function? A:

Keep in mind that the recent compiler versions and recent standards mostly haven't made it into common usage. Completeness is relative - there are compiler bugs popping up in some rarer situations, especially on newer major versions. You may be better off going with GCC 14 than GCC 15.

Honestly, if Windows is the biggest obstacle, you can look into Linux as a standalone side OS. You don't even need to install it for your use case, just make a live USB of some recent distro (Ubuntu 25.04 seems fine) and use it as your playground - you can boot it on some trash laptop on the side.

Also, if you want to learn modern C++, don't start with the most recent features. Work your way through the most crucial ones like smart pointers, polymorphism, template metaprogramming, copy vs move... when you say you learned in a C-like way, that means you should start with C++11.
